plain: Paid or persuaded to lie under oath or do a wrong

webster.text: Procured to take a false oath, or to do a bad action.

example.quote: Where there is an appeal from an inferior to a superio court, with respect to matters of fact, a new witness may be introduced, who is perhaps suborned by the other party, a thousand miles from the place where the first trial was had.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 18, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
